project_metadata.name: JDAR — Judicial Decision-Aligned Reasoning
project_metadata.paper_type_final: audit / analysis paper with negative headline result

thesis.originating_question: Why do LLMs reason over legal language like ordinary language, when it carries depth, extended context, factual grounding, and pragmatic inference?
thesis.research_question: Can a model pragmatically infer the operative meaning of a contractual clause the way a court would?
thesis.current_statement: Corpus-grounded automatic preference construction for contractual clause interpretation produces pairs whose chosen and rejected members are semantically near-equivalent, and preference optimization over them yields a discriminator no better than lexical overlap — indicating that threshold-based pipeline supervision does not encode the pragmatic distinctions it is intended to capture.
falsifiers: expert annotation showing chosen is genuinely judicially superior at high agreement
any scorer exceeding ~65% on held-out pairs
decisive-tail shown to reflect interpretive rather than threshold distinctions

rejected_framings.reason: scores nothing at training or inference; filtered a dataset once, offline

rejected_framings.framing: JDAR is a verifier, not a Bradley-Terry reward model

sources.judicial_text: Harvard COLD Cases (~8.36M opinions, streamed from HuggingFace)

build_dpo_pairs.py.rejected_definition: retrieved judicial raw_sentence window with total_score < 2 and d1_anchor_vagueness == 1

triplet_quality_scorer.py.score_dimension_3: signature (anchor, sentence) — anchor x candidate; checks candidate for terms from anchor's vagueness category (scope/knowledge/necessity/etc.)

pipeline_verified_from_source.critical_finding: No step in the pipeline ever compared chosen against rejected. Supervisory signal is cleared-threshold vs did-not-clear, NOT adjudicated judicial preference.

experiments.name: lexical baselines vs stored bi_encoder_score
experiments.metric: pairwise ranking accuracy, chosen above rejected against anchor; ties count as loss
experiments.interpretation: Only two defensible statements: TF-IDF weakly beats chance on majority category; stored bi-encoder score does not discriminate. Minority categories underpowered (CI ±10-11).

experiments.name: fresh cosine recompute
experiments.interpretation: Rules out circularity. Had anchor-candidate cosine been the selection criterion this would return ~100%.

experiments.name: isotropy control (PIVOTAL)
experiments.setup: 500 random pairs of unrelated judicial windows, different anchors, different categories
experiments.interpretation: Near-isotropic. Dynamic range ~0.07-0.85. Refutes anisotropy hypothesis; whitening cancelled as unnecessary. Simultaneously STRENGTHENS main finding: chosen and rejected at 0.604 in this space are near-paraphrases.

experiments.name: DPO implicit reward, held out
experiments.setup: 500 pairs from the 2053 unused eligible negatives; r(x,y)=beta*(logp_policy - logp_ref); SFT checkpoint as reference
experiments.unexplored: mean gap is 3x median — right-skewed. Half of held-out pairs have near-zero gap; aggregate carried by a minority tail. Model is indifferent on most pairs, decisive on a few.
